body.text: jagajjanmādikāraṇaṃ brahma vedāntavedyam ity uktam / tad ayuktam; tad dhi na vākyapratipādyam / anumānena siddheḥ ity āśaṅkyāha --
body.translated_text: It has been stated that <s>Brahman</s>, the cause of the origination and so forth of the world, is to be known through <s>Vedānta</s>. [Objection:] This is inappropriate, for it is not something to be established by scriptural sentences, since it can be established by inference. Anticipating this objection, [the <s>sūtrakāra</s>] says:

children.text: jagaj-janma-ādi-kāraṇaṃ brahma vedānta-vedyam ity uktam / tad ayuktam; tad dhi na vākya-pratipādyam / anumānena siddheḥ ity āśaṅkyā aha ---

body.text: śāstrayonitvāt //
body.translated_text: Because [<s>Brahman</s>] has scripture as its source (<s>śāstrayonitvāt</s>).

children.text: śāstra-yonitvāt //

body.text: śastraṃ yasya yoniḥ -- kāraṇaṃ, pramāṇam, tac chāstrayoniḥ; tasya bhāvaś śāstrayonitvam; tasmāt /
body.translated_text: That of which scripture (<s>śāstra</s>) is the source (<s>yoni</s>) — that is, the cause, the means of valid knowledge (<s>pramāṇa</s>) — is <s>śāstrayoni</s>; the state of being that is <s>śāstrayonitva</s>; because of that [<s>Brahman</s> is to be known through <s>Vedānta</s>].

children.text: śastraṃ yasya yoniḥ --- kāraṇaṃ, pramāṇam, tac chāstra-yoniḥ; tasya bhāvaś śāstra-yonitvam; tasmāt /

body.text: brahmajñānakāraṇatvāc chāstrasya tadyonitvaṃ brahmaṇaḥ / atyantātīndriyatvena pratyakṣādipramāṇāviṣayatayā brahmaṇaś śāstraikapramāṇakatvād uktasvarūpaṃ brahma yato vā imāni bhūtānītyādivākyaṃ bodhayaty evetyarthaḥ //
body.translated_text: Because scripture is the cause of the knowledge of <s>Brahman</s>, <s>Brahman</s> has scripture as its source. Since <s>Brahman</s> is utterly beyond the senses and thus not within the scope of perception (<s>pratyakṣa</s>) and other means of valid knowledge, <s>Brahman</s> is knowable solely through scripture. The meaning is that the <s>Vedāntic</s> sentence 'from which indeed these beings [are born]' and the like necessarily conveys [the knowledge of] <s>Brahman</s> whose nature has been stated.

children.text: brahma-jñāna-kāraṇatvāc chāstrasya tad-yonitvaṃ brahmaṇaḥ / atyanta-atīndriyatvena pratyakṣa-ādi-pramāṇa-aviṣayatayā brahmaṇaś śāstra-eka-pramāṇakatvād ukta-svarūpaṃ brahma yato vā imāni bhūtāni ity-ādi-vākyaṃ bodhayaty eva ity-arthaḥ //

body.text: nanu śāstrayonitvaṃ brahmaṇo na saṃbhavati, pramāṇāntaravedyatvād brahaṇaḥ, aprāpte tu śāstram arthavat / kiṃ tarhi tatra pramāṇam? na tāvatpratyakṣam / tad dhi dvividham -- indriyasaṃbhavaṃ yogasaṃbhavaṃ ceti / indriyasaṃbhavaṃ ca bāhyasaṃbhavam āntarasaṃbhavaṃ ceti dvividhā / bāhyendriyāṇi vidyamānasannikarṣayogyasvaviṣayabodhajananānīti na sarvārthasākṣātkāratannirmāṇasamarthapuruṣaviśeṣaviṣayabodhajananāni / nāpy āntaram; āntarasukhaduḥkhādivyatiriktabahirviṣayeṣu tasya bāhyendriyānapekṣapravṛttyanupapatteḥ / nāpi yogajanyam; bhāvanāprakarṣaparyantajanmanas tasya viśadāvabhāsatve 'pi pūrvānubhūtaviṣayasmṛtimātratvān na prāmāṇyam iti kutaḥ pratyakṣatā ? tadatiriktaviṣayatve kāraṇābhāvāt; tathā sati tasya bhramarūpavatā / nāpy anumānaṃ viśeṣatodṛṣṭaṃ sāmānyatodṛṣṭaṃ vā / atīndriye vastuni saṃbandhāvadhāraṇavirahān na viśeṣatodṛṣṭam / samastavastusākṣātkāratannirmāṇasamarthapuruṣaviśeṣaniyataṃ sāmānyatodṛṣṭam api na liṅgam upalabhayte /
body.translated_text: [Objection:] But <s>śāstrayonitva</s> (having scripture as its source) is not possible for <s>Brahman</s>, because <s>Brahman</s> is knowable through other means of valid knowledge; scripture is meaningful only where those other means do not reach. What then is the means of valid knowledge there? Not, first of all, perception (<s>pratyakṣa</s>). For that is of two kinds: sense-born and yoga-born. Sense-born perception is again of two kinds: external and internal. The external sense organs, being capable of generating cognition only of their own respective objects with which present contact is possible, are not capable of generating cognition of a special <s>Puruṣa</s> (Supreme Person) who is capable of directly perceiving all things and creating them. Nor is internal [perception sufficient], for it is impossible for internal perception to operate independently of the external sense organs with respect to external objects other than pleasure, pain, and the like [which are its proper domain]. Nor is yoga-born [perception valid here]; for although it has vivid manifestation as the culmination of intense meditation (<s>bhāvanā</s>), since it is merely a memory of previously experienced objects, it has no validity (<s>prāmāṇya</s>) — how then could it be perception? If it had objects beyond [previously experienced ones], there would be no cause [for such cognition]; and in that case, it would be of the nature of error. Nor is inference (<s>anumāna</s>) [a valid means here], whether specific (<s>viśeṣatodṛṣṭa</s>) or general (<s>sāmānyatodṛṣṭa</s>). In the case of a supra-sensory entity, specific inference is not possible due to the absence of ascertaining an invariable connection (<s>sambandha</s>). And no inferential mark (<s>liṅga</s>) is found that is invariably connected with a special <s>Puruṣa</s> capable of directly perceiving all things and creating them, [which would serve as] general inference.

children.text: nanu śāstra-yonitvaṃ brahmaṇo na saṃbhavati, pramāṇa-antara-vedyatvād brahaṇaḥ, aprāpte tu śāstram arthavat / kiṃ tarhi tatra pramāṇam? na tāvat-pratyakṣam / tad dhi dvi-vidham --- indriya-saṃbhavaṃ yoga-saṃbhavaṃ ca iti / indriya-saṃbhavaṃ ca bāhya-saṃbhavam āntara-saṃbhavaṃ ca iti dvi-vidhā / bāhya-indriyāṇi vidyamāna-sannikarṣa-yogya-sva-viṣaya-bodha-jananāni iti na sarva-artha-sākṣātkāra-tan-nirmāṇa-samartha-puruṣa-viśeṣa-viṣaya-bodha-jananāni / na apy āntaram; āntara-sukha-duḥkha-ādi-vyatirikta-bahir-viṣayeṣu tasya bāhya-indriya-anapekṣa-pravṛtty-anupapatteḥ / na api yoga-janyam; bhāvanā-prakarṣa-paryanta-janmanas tasya viśada-avabhāsatve 'pi pūrva-anubhūta-viṣaya-smṛti-mātratvān na prāmāṇyam iti kutaḥ pratyakṣatā ? tad-atirikta-viṣayatve kāraṇa-abhāvāt; tathā sati tasya bhrama-rūpavatā / na apy anumānaṃ viśeṣato-dṛṣṭaṃ sāmānyato-dṛṣṭaṃ vā / atīndriye vastuni saṃbandha-avadhāraṇa-virahān na viśeṣato-dṛṣṭam / samasta-vastu-sākṣātkāra-tan-nirmāṇa-samartha-puruṣa-viśeṣa-niyataṃ sāmānyato-dṛṣṭam api na liṅgam upalabhayte /

body.text: nanu ca jagataḥ kāryatvaṃ tadupādānopakaraṇasaṃpradānaprayojanābhijñakartṛkatvavyāptam / acetanārabdhaṃm jagataś caikacetanādhīnatvena vyāptam / sarvaṃ hi ghaṭādikāryaṃ tadupādānopakaraṇasaṃpradānaprayojanābhijñakartṛkaṃ dṛṣṭam / acetanārabdham arogaṃ svaśarīram ekacetanādhīnaṃ ca / sāvayavatvena jagataḥ kāryatvam /
body.translated_text: [Objection:] But the world's being an effect is pervaded by its having a maker who knows the material cause, instruments, endowment, and purpose [of creation]. And the world's being begun by a non-conscious [cause] is pervaded by its being dependent on a single conscious being. For every effect such as a pot is observed to have a maker who knows its material cause, instruments, endowment, and purpose. And one's own body, though not begun [deliberately] by a conscious being, is healthy and dependent on a single conscious being. And the world is an effect because it has parts (<s>sāvayavatva</s>).

children.text: nanu ca jagataḥ kāryatvaṃ tad-upādāna-upakaraṇa-saṃpradāna-prayojana-abhijña-kartṛkatva-vyāptam / acetana-ārabdhaṃm jagataś ca eka-cetana-adhīnatvena vyāptam / sarvaṃ hi ghaṭa-ādi-kāryaṃ tad-upādāna-upakaraṇa-saṃpradāna-prayojana-abhijña-kartṛkaṃ dṛṣṭam / acetana-ārabdham arogaṃ sva-śarīram eka-cetana-adhīnaṃ ca / sa-avayavatvena jagataḥ kāryatvam /

body.text: ucyate / kim idam ekacetanādhīnatvam ? na tāvat tadāyattotpattisthititvam; dṛṣṭānto hi sādhyavikalaḥ syāt / na hy arogaṃ svaśarīram ekacetanāyattotpattisthiti; taccharīrasya bhoktṝṇāṃ bhāryādisarvacenatānām adṛṣṭajanyatvāt tadutpattisthityoḥ / kiṃ ca, śarīrāvayavinaḥ svāvayavasamavetatārūpā sthitir avayavasaṃśleṣavyatirekeṇa na cetanam apekṣate / prāṇanalakṣaṇā tu sthitiḥ pakṣatvābhimate kṣitijaladhimahīdharādau na saṃbhavatīti pakṣasapakṣānugatām ekarūpāṃ sthitiṃ nopalabhāmahe / tad āyattapravṛttitvaṃ tadadhīnatvam iti cet, anekacetanasādhyeṣu gurutararathaśilāmahīruhādiṣu vyabhicāraḥ / cetanamātrādhīnatve siddhasādhyatā /
body.translated_text: [Reply:] We say: What is this 'dependence on a single conscious being'? It is not, first of all, having its origination and persistence dependent on that [single conscious being]; for then the illustrative example would lack the property to be proved. For one's own healthy body does not have its origination and persistence dependent on a single conscious being, since the bodies of the experiencers — wives, and all other conscious beings — are produced by <s>adṛṣṭa</s> (unseen merit/demerit), and so are their origination and persistence. Moreover, the persistence of a composite body — which is of the nature of a configuration inhering in its parts — does not require a conscious being apart from the cohesion of its parts. But persistence characterized by vitality (<s>prāṇana</s>) does not occur in the earth, waters, mountains, and the like, which are claimed as the subject [of inference] — thus we do not find a single uniform kind of persistence that is common to both the subject and the corroborating instances. If [you say that] 'dependence on that' means 'having activity dependent on that' — then there is deviation (<s>vyabhicāra</s>) in things accomplished by multiple conscious beings, such as heavy chariots, rocks, great trees, and the like. If [the inference is that there is] dependence merely on some conscious being, then [the conclusion is] already established (<s>siddhasādhyatā</s>).

children.text: ucyate / kim idam eka-cetana-adhīnatvam ? na tāvat tad-āyatta-utpatti-sthititvam; dṛṣṭānto hi sādhya-vikalaḥ syāt / na hy arogaṃ sva-śarīram eka-cetana-āyatta-utpatti-sthiti; tac-charīrasya bhoktṝṇāṃ bhārya-ādi-sarva-cenatānām adṛṣṭa-janyatvāt tad-utpatti-sthityoḥ / kiṃ ca, śarīra-avayavinaḥ sva-avayava-samavetatā-rūpā sthitir avayava-saṃśleṣa-vyatirekeṇa na cetanam apekṣate / prāṇana-lakṣaṇā tu sthitiḥ pakṣatva-abhimate kṣiti-jaladhi-mahīdhara-ādau na saṃbhavati iti pakṣa-sapakṣa-anugatām eka-rūpāṃ sthitiṃ na upalabhāmahe / tad -āyatta-pravṛttitvaṃ tad-adhīnatvam iti cet, aneka-cetana-sādhyeṣu guru-tara-ratha-śilā-mahīruha-ādiṣu vyabhicāraḥ / cetana-mātra-adhīnatve siddha-sādhyatā /

body.text: kiṃ ca, ubhayavādisiddhānāṃ jīvānām eva lāghavena kartṛtvābhyupagamo yuktaḥ / na ca jīvānām upādānādyanabhijñatayā kartṛtvāsaṃbhavaḥ; sarveṣām eva cetanānāṃ pṛthivyādyupādānayāgādyupakaraṇasākṣātkārasāmarthyāt; yathedānīṃ pṛthivyādayo yāgādayaś ca pratyakṣam īkṣyante / upakaraṇabhūtayāgādiśaktirūpāpūrvādiśabdavācyādṛṣṭasākṣātkārābhāve 'pi cetanānāṃ na kartṛtvānupapattiḥ; tatsākṣātkārānapekṣaṇāt kāryārambhasya / bhaktimatsākṣātkāra eva hi kāryārambhopayogī; śaktes tu jñānamātram evopayujyate, na sākṣātkāraḥ / na hi kulālādayaḥ kāryopakaraṇabhūtadaṇḍacakrādivat tacchaktim api sākṣātkṛtya ghaṭamaṇikādikāryam ārabhante / iha tu cetanānām āgamāvagatayāgādiśaktiviśeṣāṇāṃ kāryārambho nānupapannaḥ /
body.translated_text: Moreover, it is proper to accept, by the principle of parsimony, that the individual souls (<s>jīvas</s>) alone — accepted by both parties in the debate — are the agents [of creation]. Nor is the agency of <s>jīvas</s> impossible due to their ignorance of material causes and the like, since all conscious beings have the capacity to directly perceive material causes such as earth and the like, and instrumental causes such as sacrifices and the like — just as earth and the like, and sacrifices and the like, are now seen by direct perception. Even without the direct perception of the unseen [force] (<s>adṛṣṭa</s>), referred to by the term <s>apūrva</s> and the like, which has the nature of the power of sacrifices and other means — the agency of conscious beings is not impossible, because the commencement of an effect does not depend upon direct perception of that [unseen force]. For it is direct perception accompanied by devotion alone that is useful for commencing an effect; but for the power [of the sacrifice], only knowledge of it is required, not direct perception. For potters and the like do not commence the production of pots, gems, and the like only after directly perceiving the power [inherent in] the staff, wheel, and the like that are instrumental causes. Here, however, the commencement of effects by conscious beings who know the specific powers of sacrifices and the like through scripture is not impossible.

children.text: kiṃ ca, ubhaya-vādi-siddhānāṃ jīvānām eva lāghavena kartṛtva-abhyupagamo yuktaḥ / na ca jīvānām upādāna-ādy-anabhijñatayā kartṛtva-asaṃbhavaḥ; sarveṣām eva cetanānāṃ pṛthivy-ādy-upādāna-yāga-ādy-upakaraṇa-sākṣātkāra-sāmarthyāt; yatha īdānīṃ pṛthivy-ādayo yāga-ādayaś ca pratyakṣam īkṣyante / upakaraṇa-bhūta-yāga-ādi-śakti-rūpa-apūrva-ādi-śabda-vācya-adṛṣṭa-sākṣātkāra-abhāve 'pi cetanānāṃ na kartṛtva-anupapattiḥ; tat-sākṣātkāra-anapekṣaṇāt kārya-ārambhasya / bhaktimat-sākṣātkāra eva hi kārya-ārambha-upayogī; śaktes tu jñāna-mātram eva upayujyate, na sākṣātkāraḥ / na hi kulāla-ādayaḥ kārya-upakaraṇa-bhūta-daṇḍa-cakra-ādivat tac-chaktim api sākṣātkṛtya ghaṭa-maṇika-ādi-kāryam ārabhante / iha tu cetanānām āgama-avagata-yāga-ādi-śakti-viśeṣāṇāṃ kārya-ārambho na anupapannaḥ /

body.text: kiṃ ca, yacchakyakriyaṃ śakyopādānādivijñānaṃ ca tad eva tadabhijñakartṛkaṃ dṛṣṭam / mahīmahīdharamahārṇavādi tv aśakyakriyam aśakyopādānādivijñānaṃ ceti na cetanakartṛkam / ato ghaṭamaṇikādi sajātīyaśakyakriyaśakyopādānādivijñānavastugatam eva kāryatvaṃ buddhimankartṛpūrvakatvasādhane prabhavati /
body.translated_text: Moreover, that which is capable of being produced and whose material causes are capable of being known — that alone is seen to have a creator who knows those [causes]. But earth, mountains, great oceans, and the like are incapable of being produced and their material causes are incapable of being known — therefore they do not have a conscious creator. Hence, the quality of effecthood, belonging only to things like pots and gems whose production is possible and whose material causes are knowable by similar beings — is effective only in proving that [such things] are preceded by an intelligent maker.

children.text: kiṃ ca, yac-chakya-kriyaṃ śakya-upādāna-ādi-vijñānaṃ ca tad eva tad-abhijña-kartṛkaṃ dṛṣṭam / mahī-mahīdhara-mahārṇava-ādi tv aśakya-kriyam aśakya-upādāna-ādi-vijñānaṃ ca iti na cetana-kartṛkam / ato ghaṭa-maṇika-ādi sajātīya-śakya-kriya-śakya-upādāna-ādi-vijñāna-vastu-gatam eva kāryatvaṃ buddhiman-kartṛ-pūrvakatva-sādhane prabhavati /

body.text: kiṃ ca, ghaṭādikāryam anīśvareṇālpajñānaśaktinā saśarīreṇa parigrahavatānāptakāmena nirmitaṃ dṛṣṭam iti tathāvidham eva cetanaṃ kartāraṃ sādhayann ayaṃ kāryatvahetus siṣādhayiṣitapuruṣasārvajñyasarvāiśvaryādiviparītasādhanād viruddhas syāt / na caitāvatā sarvānumānocchedaprasaṅgaḥ / liṅgini pramāṇāntaragocare liṅgabalopasthāpitā viparītaviśeṣās tatpramāṇapratihatagatayo nivartante / iha tu sakaletarapramāṇāviṣaye liṅgini nikhilanirmāṇacature anvayavyatirekāvagatāvinābhāvaniyamā dharmās sarva evāviśeṣeṇa prasajyante; nivartakapramāṇābhāvāt tathaivāvatiṣṭhante / ata āgamād ṛte katham īśvaras setsyati ?
body.translated_text: Moreover, effects such as pots are seen to be produced by a being who is not <s>Īśvara</s> (God), who has limited knowledge and power, who is embodied, who has possessions, and who has unfulfilled desires. Therefore, this reasoning from effecthood (<s>kāryatvahetu</s>), in establishing only such a conscious being as the creator, would be contradictory (<s>viruddha</s>) since it would prove the opposite of the intended [conclusion] — namely, the omniscience, supreme sovereignty, and the like of the Person [God]. Nor does this entail the destruction of all inference. Where the subject of inference is within the range of other means of knowledge, specific features established by the force of the inferential mark that are contrary [to those other means] are overturned by those other means of knowledge. But here, where the subject of inference is beyond the range of all other means of knowledge, all properties — established through invariable concomitance ascertained through agreement and difference — as belonging to one skilled in all creation, apply universally without distinction; and since there is no overriding means of knowledge, they remain as they are. Therefore, without scripture (<s>āgama</s>), how can <s>Īśvara</s> be established?

children.text: kiṃ ca, ghaṭa-ādi-kāryam anīśvareṇa alpa-jñāna-śaktinā sa-śarīreṇa parigrahavata ānāpta-kāmena nirmitaṃ dṛṣṭam iti tathā-vidham eva cetanaṃ kartāraṃ sādhayann ayaṃ kāryatva-hetus siṣādhayiṣita-puruṣa-sārvajñya-sarva-aiśvarya-ādi-viparīta-sādhanād viruddhas syāt / na ca etāvatā sarva-anumāna-uccheda-prasaṅgaḥ / liṅgini pramāṇa-antara-gocare liṅga-bala-upasthāpitā viparīta-viśeṣās tat-pramāṇa-pratihata-gatayo nivartante / iha tu sakala-itara-pramāṇa-aviṣaye liṅgini nikhila-nirmāṇa-cature anvaya-vyatireka-avagata-avinābhāva-niyamā dharmās sarva eva aviśeṣeṇa prasajyante; nivartaka-pramāṇa-abhāvāt tatha aiva avatiṣṭhante / ata āgamād ṛte katham īśvaras setsyati ?

body.text: atrāhuḥ / sāvayavatvād eva jagataḥ kāryatvaṃ na pratyākhyātuṃ śakyate / bhavanti ca prayogāḥ -- vivādādhyāsitaṃ bhūbhūdharādi kāryam, sāvayavatvāt, ghaṭādivat / tathā vivādādhyāsitam avanijaladhimahīdharādi kāryam, mahattve sati kriyāvattvāt, ghaṭavat / tanubhuvanādi kāryam, mahattve sati mūrtatvāt, ghaṭavat -- iti / sāvayaveṣu dravyeṣu idam eva kriyate netarad iti kāryatvasya niyāmakaṃ sāvayavatvātireki rūpāntaraṃ nopalabhāmahe / kāryatvapratiniyataṃ śakyakriyatvaṃ śakyopādānādivijñānatvaṃ copalabhyata iti cen na; kāryatvenānumate 'pi viṣaye jñānaśaktī kāryānumeye ity anyatrāpi sāvayavatvādinā kāryatvaṃ jñātam iti te ca pratipanne eveti na kaścid viśeṣaḥ / tathā hi ghaṭamaṇikādiṣu kṛteṣu kāryadarśanānumitakartṛgatatannirmāṇaśaktijñānaḥ puruṣo 'dṛṣṭapūrvaṃ vicitrasanniveśaṃ narendrabhavanam ālokya avayavasanniveṣaviśeṣeṇa tasya kāryatvaṃ niścitya tadānīm eva kartus tajjñānaśaktivaicitryam anuminoti / atas tanubhuvanādeḥ kāryatve siddhe sarvasākṣātkāratannirmāṇādinipuṇaḥ kvacit puruṣaviśeṣas sidhyaty eva /
body.translated_text: To this they reply: The effecthood of the world cannot be denied simply because it has parts (<s>sāvayavatva</s>). And the following syllogisms are adduced: 'The earth, mountains, etc. — which are the subjects of dispute — are effects, because they have parts, like a pot.' Likewise: 'The earth, oceans, mountains, etc. — which are the subjects of dispute — are effects, because they possess activity while being great in size, like a pot.' And: 'The body, the universe, etc. are effects, because they are material while being great in size, like a pot.' We do not perceive any additional characteristic beyond having parts that determines effecthood, such that in substances having parts, only this [effecthood] would obtain and nothing else. If it be objected that what is invariably associated with effecthood is the possibility of production and the knowability of material causes — this is not so. For even when effecthood is conceded in a given case, knowledge and power are inferred from the effect. And since effecthood has already been established elsewhere too through having parts and the like, those [knowledge and power] too are already conceded — so there is no difference. For example, a person who has inferred the creator's knowledge and skill in construction from observing the production of pots, gems, and the like — upon beholding a king's palace of unprecedented and marvelous design — ascertains its effecthood from the particular arrangement of its parts and immediately infers the variety of the creator's knowledge and skill. Therefore, once the effecthood of the body, the universe, and the like is established, some special Person (<s>puruṣaviśeṣa</s>) who directly perceives everything and is skilled in its creation is indeed established.

children.text: atrā ahuḥ / sa-avayavatvād eva jagataḥ kāryatvaṃ na pratyākhyātuṃ śakyate / bhavanti ca prayogāḥ --- vivāda-adhyāsitaṃ bhū-bhūdhara-ādi kāryam, sa-avayavatvāt, ghaṭa-ādivat / tathā vivāda-adhyāsitam avani-jaladhi-mahīdhara-ādi kāryam, mahattve sati kriyāvattvāt, ghaṭavat / tanu-bhuvana-ādi kāryam, mahattve sati mūrtatvāt, ghaṭavat --- iti / sa-avayaveṣu dravyeṣu idam eva kriyate na itarad iti kāryatvasya niyāmakaṃ sa-avayavatva-atireki rūpa-antaraṃ na upalabhāmahe / kāryatva-pratiniyataṃ śakya-kriyatvaṃ śakya-upādāna-ādi-vijñānatvaṃ ca upalabhyata iti cen na; kāryatvena anumate 'pi viṣaye jñāna-śaktī kārya-anumeye ity anyatra api sa-avayavatva-ādinā kāryatvaṃ jñātam iti te ca pratipanne eva iti na kaścid viśeṣaḥ / tathā hi ghaṭa-maṇika-ādiṣu kṛteṣu kārya-darśana-anumita-kartṛ-gata-tan-nirmāṇa-śakti-jñānaḥ puruṣo 'dṛṣṭa-pūrvaṃ vicitra-sanniveśaṃ nara-indra-bhavanam ālokya avayava-sanniveṣa-viśeṣeṇa tasya kāryatvaṃ niścitya tadānīm eva kartus taj-jñāna-śakti-vaicitryam anuminoti / atas tanu-bhuvana-ādeḥ kāryatve siddhe sarva-sākṣātkāra-tan-nirmāṇa-ādi-nipuṇaḥ kvacit puruṣa-viśeṣas sidhyaty eva /

body.text: kiṃ ca sarvacetanānāṃ dharmādharmanimitte 'pi sukhaduḥkhopabhoge cetanānadhiṣṭhitayos tayor acetanayoḥ phalahetutvānupapattes sarvakarmānuguṇasarvaphalapradānacaturaḥ kaścid āstheyaḥ; vardhakinānadhiṣṭhitasya vāsyāder acetanasya deśakālādyanekaparikarasannidhāne 'pi yūpādinirmāṇasādhanatvādarśanāt / bījāṅkuarādeḥ pakṣāntarbhāvena tair vyabhicārāpādanaṃ śrotriyavetālānām anabhijñatāvijṛmbhitam / tata eva sukhādibhir vyabhicāravacanam api tathaiva / na ca lāghavenobhayavādisaṃpratipannakṣetrajñānām eva īdṛśādhiṣṭhātṛtvakalpanaṃ yuktam; teṣāṃ sūkṣmavyavahitaviprakṛṣṭadarśanaśaktiniścayāt / darśanānuguṇaiva hi sarvatra kalpanā / na ca kṣetrajñavad īśvarasyāśaktiniścayo 'sti / ataḥ prāmāṇāntaro na tatsiddhyanupapattiḥ / samarthakartṛpūrvakatvaniyatakāryatvahetunā sidhyan svābhāvikasarvasākṣātkāratanniyamanaśaktisaṃpanna eva sidhyati /

children.text: kiṃ ca sarva-cetanānāṃ dharma-adharma-nimitte 'pi sukha-duḥkha-upabhoge cetana-anadhiṣṭhitayos tayor acetanayoḥ phala-hetutva-anupapattes sarva-karma-anuguṇa-sarva-phala-pradāna-caturaḥ kaścid āstheyaḥ; vardhakina ānadhiṣṭhitasya vāsya-āder acetanasya deśa-kāla-ādy-aneka-parikara-sannidhāne 'pi yūpa-ādi-nirmāṇa-sādhanatva-adarśanāt / bīja-aṅkuar-ādeḥ pakṣa-antarbhāvena tair vyabhicāra-āpādanaṃ śrotriya-vetālānām anabhijñatā-vijṛmbhitam / tata eva sukha-ādibhir vyabhicāra-vacanam api tatha aiva / na ca lāghavena ubhaya-vādi-saṃpratipanna-kṣetra-jñānām eva īdṛśa-adhiṣṭhātṛtva-kalpanaṃ yuktam; teṣāṃ sūkṣma-vyavahita-viprakṛṣṭa-darśana-śakti-niścayāt / darśana-anuguṇa aiva hi sarvatra kalpanā / na ca kṣetra-jñavad īśvarasya aśakti-niścayo 'sti / ataḥ prāmāṇa-antaro na tat-siddhy-anupapattiḥ / samartha-kartṛ-pūrvakatva-niyata-kāryatva-hetunā sidhyan svābhāvika-sarva-sākṣātkāra-tan-niyamana-śakti-saṃpanna eva sidhyati /

body.text: yat tv anaiśvaryādyāpādanena dharmaviśeṣaviparītasādhanatvam unnītam, tadanumānavṛttānabhijñatvanibandhanam; sapakṣe sahadṛṣṭānāṃ sarveṣāṃ kāryasyāhetubhūtānāṃ ca dharmāṇāṃ liṅginy aprāpteḥ / etad uktaṃ bhavati / kenacit kiṃcit kriyamāṇaṃ svotpattaye kartus svanirmāṇasāmarthyaṃ svopādānopakaraṇajñānaṃ cāpekṣate; na tv anyāsāmarthyam anyajñānaṃ ca, hetutvābhāvāt / svanirmāṇasāmarthyasvopādānopakaraṇajñānābhyām eva svotpattāv upapannāyāṃ saṃbandhitayā darśanamātreṇākiṃcitkarasyārthāntarājñānādeḥ hetutvakalpanāyogād iti / na tāvat sarvaviṣayam; na hi kulālādiḥ kriyamāṇavyatiriktaṃ kim api na jānāti / nāpi katipayaviṣayam; sarveṣu kartṛṣu tattadajñānāśaktyaniyamena sarveṣām ajñānādīnāṃ vyabhicārāt / ataḥ kāryatvasyāsādhakānām anīśvaratvādīnāṃ liṅginy apratītir iti na viparītasādhanatvam /

children.text: yat tv anaiśvarya-ādy-āpādanena dharma-viśeṣa-viparīta-sādhanatvam unnītam, tad-anumāna-vṛtta-anabhijñatva-nibandhanam; sapakṣe saha-dṛṣṭānāṃ sarveṣāṃ kāryasya ahetu-bhūtānāṃ ca dharmāṇāṃ liṅginy aprāpteḥ / etad uktaṃ bhavati / kenacit kiṃcit kriyamāṇaṃ sva-utpattaye kartus sva-nirmāṇa-sāmarthyaṃ sva-upādāna-upakaraṇa-jñānaṃ ca apekṣate; na tv anya-asāmarthyam anya-jñānaṃ ca, hetutva-abhāvāt / sva-nirmāṇa-sāmarthya-sva-upādāna-upakaraṇa-jñānābhyām eva sva-utpattāv upapannāyāṃ saṃbandhitayā darśana-mātreṇa akiṃcitkarasya artha-antara-ajñāna-ādeḥ hetutva-kalpanā-yogād iti / na tāvat sarva-viṣayam; na hi kulāla-ādiḥ kriyamāṇa-vyatiriktaṃ kim api na jānāti / na api katipaya-viṣayam; sarveṣu kartṛṣu tat-tad-ajñāna-aśakty-aniyamena sarveṣām ajñāna-ādīnāṃ vyabhicārāt / ataḥ kāryatvasya asādhakānām anīśvaratva-ādīnāṃ liṅginy apratītir iti na viparīta-sādhanatvam /

body.text: kulālādīnāṃ daṇḍacakrādyadhiṣṭhānaṃ śarīradvāreṇaiva dṛṣṭam iti jagadupādānopakaraṇādhiṣṭhānam īśvarasyā-śarīrasyānupapannam iti cen na; saṃkalpamātreṇaiva paraśarīragatabhūtavetālagaralādyapagamavināśadarśanāt / katham aśarīrasya parapravartanarūpas saṃkalpa iti cet; na śarīrāpekṣas saṃkalpaḥ, śarīrasya saṃkalpahetutvābhāvāt / mana eva hi saṃkalpahetuḥ / tadabhyupagatam īśvare 'pi; kāryatvenaiva jñānaśaktivan manaso 'pi prāptatvāt / mānasas saṃkalpas saśarīrasyaiva, saśarīrasyaiva samanaskatvād iti cen na; manaso nityatvena dehāpagame 'pi manasas sadbhāvenānaikāntyāt /

children.text: kulāla-ādīnāṃ daṇḍa-cakra-ādy-adhiṣṭhānaṃ śarīra-dvāreṇa eva dṛṣṭam iti jagad-upādāna-upakaraṇa-adhiṣṭhānam īśvarasya a-śarīrasya anupapannam iti cen na; saṃkalpa-mātreṇa eva para-śarīra-gata-bhūta-vetāla-garala-ādy-apagama-vināśa-darśanāt / katham a-śarīrasya para-pravartana-rūpas saṃkalpa iti cet; na śarīra-apekṣas saṃkalpaḥ, śarīrasya saṃkalpa-hetu-tva-abhāvāt / mana eva hi saṃkalpa-hetuḥ / tad-abhyupagatam īśvare 'pi; kāryatvena eva jñāna-śaktivan manaso 'pi prāptatvāt / mānasas saṃkalpas sa-śarīrasya eva, sa-śarīrasya eva sa-manaskatvād iti cen na; manaso nityatvena deha-apagame 'pi manasas sad-bhāvena anaikāntyāt /

body.text: ato vicitrāvayavasanniveśaviśeṣatanubhuvanādikāryanirmāṇe puṇyapāpaparavaśaḥ parimitaśaktijñānaḥ kṣetrajño na prabhavatīti nikhilabhuvananirmāṇacaturo 'cintyāparimitajñānaśaktyaiśvaryo 'śarīraḥ saṃkalpamātrasādhanapariniṣpannānantavistāravicitraracanaprapañcaḥ puruṣaviśeṣa īśvaro 'numānenaiva siddhyati / ataḥ pramāṇāntarāvaseyatvād brahmaṇo naitadvākyaṃ brahma pratipādayati /

evaṃ prāpte brūmaḥ -- yathoktalakṣaṇaṃ brahma janmādivākyaṃ bodhayaty eva / kutaḥ? śāstraikapramāṇakatvād brahmaṇaḥ / yad uktaṃ sāvayavatvādinā kāryaṃ sarvaṃ jagat, kāryaṃ ca taducitakartṛviśeṣapūrvakaṃ dṛṣṭam iti nikhilajagannirmāṇatadupādānopakaraṇavedanacaturaḥ kaścid anumeya iti; tad ayuktam; mahīmahārṇavādīnāṃ kāryatve 'pi ekadaivaikenaiva nirmitā ity atra pramāṇābhāvāt / na caikasya ghaṭasyeva sarveṣām ekaṃ kāryatvam, yenaikadaikaḥ kartā syāt / pṛthagbhūteṣu kāryeṣu kālabhedakartṛbhedadarśanena kartṛkālāikyaniyamādarśanāt / na ca kṣetrajñānāṃ vicitrajagannirmāṇaśaktyā kāryatvabalena tadatiriktakalpanāyām anekakalpanānupapatteś ca ekaḥ kartā bhavitum arhatīti; kṣetrajñānām evopacitapuṇyaviśeṣāṇāṃ śaktivaicitryadarśanena teṣām evātiśayitādṛṣṭasaṃbhāvanayā ca tattadvilakṣaṇakāryahetutvasaṃbhavāt, tadatiriktātyantādṛṣṭapuruṣakalpanānupapatteḥ / na ca yugapat sarvotpattis sarvocchittiś ca pramāṇapadavīm adhirohataḥ; adarśanāt, krameṇaivotpattivināśadarśanāc ca / kāryatvena sarvotpattivināśayoḥ kalpyamānayoḥ darśanānuguṇyena kalpanāyāṃ virodhābhāvāc ca / ato buddhimadekakartṛkatve sādhye kāryatvasyānaikāntyam, pakṣasyāprasiddhaviśeṣaṇatvam, sādhyavikalatā ca dṛṣṭāntasya; sarvanirmāṇacaturasyaikasyāprasiddheḥ / buddhimatkartṛkatvamātre sādhye siddhasādhanatā / sārvajñyasarvaśaktiyuktasya kasyacid ekasya sādhakam idaṃ kāryatvaṃ kiṃ yugamadutpadyamānasarvavastugatam ? uta krameṇotpadyamānasarvavāstugatam ? yugapadutpadyamānasarvavastugatatve kāryatvasyāsiddhatā / krameṇotpadyamānasarvavastugatatve anekakarṭrkatvasādhanād viruddhatā / atrāpy ekakarṭrkatvasādhane pratyakṣānumānavirodhaś śāstravirodhaś ca; kumbhakāro
jāyate, rathakāro jāyata ityādiśravaṇāt / api ca sarveṣāṃ kāryāṇāṃ śarīrādīnāṃ ca sattvādiguṇakāryarūpasukhādyanvayadarśanena sattvādimūlatvam avaśyāśrayaṇīyam / kāryavaicitryahetubhūtāḥ kāraṇagatā viśeṣās sattvādayaḥ; teṣāṃ kāryāṇāṃ tanmūlatvāpādanaṃ tadyuktapuruṣāntaḥkaraṇavikāradvāreṇa, puruṣasya ca tadyogaḥ karmamūlaḥ -- iti kāryaviśeṣārambhāyaiva jñānaśaktivat kartuḥ karmasaṃbandhaḥ kāryahetutvenaivāvaśyāśrayanīyaḥ; jñānaśaktivaicitryasya ca karmamūlatvāt / icchāyāḥ kāryārambhahetutve 'pi viṣayaviśeṣaviśeṣitāyās tasyās sattvāimūlakatvena karmasaṃbandho 'varjanīyaḥ / ataḥ kṣetrajñā eva kartāraḥ, na tadvilakṣaṇaḥ kaścid anumānāt sidhyati / bhavanti ca prayogāḥ -- tanubhuvanādi kṣetrajñakartṛkam, kāryatvāt, ghaṭavat / īśvaraḥ kartā na bhavati, prayojanaśūnyatvāt, muktātmavat / īśvaraḥ kartā na bhavati, aśarīratvāt, tadvad eva / na ca kṣetrajñānāṃ svaśarīrādhiṣṭhāne vyabhicāraḥ, tatrāpy anādes sūkṣmaśarīrasta sadbhāvāt/ vimativiṣayaḥ kālo na lokaśūnyaḥ, kālatvāt, vartamānakālavad iti /
body.translated_text: This being the prima facie position, we reply: the statement about origin and the like does indeed convey <s>Brahman</s> as having the characteristics described. Why? Because <s>Brahman</s> is knowable only through scripture (<s>śāstra</s>). It has been argued that the entire world, being possessed of parts and the like, is an effect; and that an effect is seen to presuppose a particular agent suited to it; therefore some being, skilled in the creation of the entire world, its material cause, instruments, and knowledge, should be inferred. But this is unjustified, because even if the earth, the great oceans, and the like are effects, there is no evidence that they were all created at one time by a single maker. Nor is the effect-nature of all things of one kind, like that of a single pot, such that there must be a single maker at one time. Since in effects that exist separately, the observation of difference in time and difference of makers [shows that] there is no rule requiring unity of maker and time. Nor can it be maintained that the individual souls (<s>kṣetrajñas</s>), possessing the power to create the variegated world, and since by the force of their being effects the postulation of something beyond them would be impossible — and since the postulation of multiple [extraordinary beings] would be inappropriate — there must be a single maker; for, since the <s>kṣetrajñas</s> themselves, with their accumulated special merits (<s>puṇya</s>), are seen to possess diversity of powers, and since by the supposition of their extraordinary unseen merit (<s>adṛṣṭa</s>) the possibility of their being causes of effects different from themselves exists, the postulation of an utterly unseen person beyond them is unjustified. Nor does the simultaneous origination and destruction of everything attain the status of valid evidence, since it is not observed, and since origination and destruction are seen to occur only gradually. And when the origination and destruction of everything is postulated through [the nature of] being effects, since there is no contradiction in postulating in accordance with what is observed. Therefore, when the thesis to be proved is that there is a single intelligent maker: the reason of 'being an effect' (<s>kāryatva</s>) is inconclusive (<s>anaikāntya</s>); the thesis has an unestablished qualifier (<s>aprasiddhaviśeṣaṇatva</s>); and the example is deficient in the property to be proved (<s>sādhyavikalatā</s>) — since a single being skilled in the creation of everything is not established. If what is to be proved is merely that there is an intelligent maker, then the proof is trivially redundant (<s>siddhasādhana</s>). Does this proof of effect-nature, [said to] establish some single being endowed with omniscience and omnipotence, apply to all things originating simultaneously? Or to all things originating gradually? If to all things originating simultaneously — the effect-nature is itself unestablished. If to all things originating gradually — there is contradiction (<s>viruddha</s>), since it would prove multiplicity of makers. Moreover, in proving a single maker here, there is contradiction with perception and inference, and contradiction with scripture — since we hear: 'A potter is born; a chariot-maker is born,' and so forth. Furthermore, since in all effects — bodies and the like — one observes the invariable concomitance of pleasure and the like, which are effects of <s>sattva</s> and the other <s>guṇas</s>, it must necessarily be accepted that [effects] are rooted in <s>sattva</s> and the rest. The particularities residing in the cause that account for the diversity of effects are <s>sattva</s> and the rest; the derivation of those effects from that root is through the modifications of the inner organ (<s>antaḥkaraṇa</s>) of a person endowed with those [guṇas]; and the person's connection with those [guṇas] is rooted in <s>karma</s>. Thus, just as knowledge and power [are related to the maker], the maker's connection with <s>karma</s> must necessarily be accepted as the cause of the effect — precisely because it is the cause of the undertaking of particular effects; and since the diversity of knowledge and power is itself rooted in <s>karma</s>. Even when desire (<s>icchā</s>) is accepted as the cause of the undertaking of an effect, since that [desire], qualified by a particular object, is rooted in <s>sattva</s> and the rest, its connection with <s>karma</s> is unavoidable. Therefore, the <s>kṣetrajñas</s> (individual souls) themselves are the makers — no one different from them is established through inference. And there are [counter-]arguments: Bodies, worlds, and the like have <s>kṣetrajñas</s> as their makers, because they are effects, like a pot. <s>Īśvara</s> (God) is not a maker, because he lacks a purpose, like a liberated soul. <s>Īśvara</s> is not a maker, because he is without a body, likewise. Nor is there any deviation [from the rule] in the <s>kṣetrajñas</s>' governance of their own bodies, since even there the beginningless subtle body exists. The time that is the subject of doubt is not devoid of [a] world, because it is time, like the present time.

children.text:
evaṃ prāpte brūmaḥ --- yatha ūkta-lakṣaṇaṃ brahma janma-ādi-vākyaṃ bodhayaty eva / kutaḥ? śāstra-eka-pramāṇakatvād brahmaṇaḥ / yad uktaṃ sa-avayavatva-ādinā kāryaṃ sarvaṃ jagat, kāryaṃ ca tad-ucita-kartṛ-viśeṣa-pūrvakaṃ dṛṣṭam iti nikhila-jagan-nirmāṇa-tad-upādāna-upakaraṇa-vedana-caturaḥ kaścid anumeya iti; tad ayuktam; mahī-mahārṇava-ādīnāṃ kāryatve 'pi ekada aiva ekena eva nirmitā ity atra pramāṇa-abhāvāt / na ca ekasya ghaṭasya iva sarveṣām ekaṃ kāryatvam, yena ekada aikaḥ kartā syāt / pṛthag-bhūteṣu kāryeṣu kāla-bheda-kartṛ-bheda-darśanena kartṛ-kāla-aikya-niyama-adarśanāt / na ca kṣetra-jñānāṃ vicitra-jagan-nirmāṇa-śaktyā kāryatva-balena tad-atirikta-kalpanāyām aneka-kalpanā-anupapatteś ca ekaḥ kartā bhavitum arhati iti; kṣetra-jñānām eva upacita-puṇya-viśeṣāṇāṃ śakti-vaicitrya-darśanena teṣām eva atiśayita-adṛṣṭa-saṃbhāvanayā ca tat-tad-vilakṣaṇa-kārya-hetutva-saṃbhavāt, tad-atirikta-atyanta-adṛṣṭa-puruṣa-kalpanā-anupapatteḥ / na ca yugapat sarva-utpattis sarva-ucchittiś ca pramāṇa-padavīm adhirohataḥ; adarśanāt, krameṇa eva utpatti-vināśa-darśanāc ca / kāryatvena sarva-utpatti-vināśayoḥ kalpyamānayoḥ darśana-ānuguṇyena kalpanāyāṃ virodha-abhāvāc ca / ato buddhimad-eka-kartṛkatve sādhye kāryatvasya anaikāntyam, pakṣasya aprasiddha-viśeṣaṇatvam, sādhya-vikalatā ca dṛṣṭāntasya; sarva-nirmāṇa-caturasya ekasya aprasiddheḥ / buddhimat-kartṛkatva-mātre sādhye siddha-sādhanatā / sārvajñya-sarva-śakti-yuktasya kasyacid ekasya sādhakam idaṃ kāryatvaṃ kiṃ yugamad-utpadyamāna-sarva-vastu-gatam ? uta krameṇa utpadyamāna-sarva-vāstu-gatam ? yugapad-utpadyamāna-sarva-vastu-gatatve kāryatvasya asiddhatā / krameṇa utpadyamāna-sarva-vastu-gatatve aneka-karṭrkatva-sādhanād viruddhatā / atra apy eka-karṭrkatva-sādhane pratyakṣa-anumāna-virodhaś śāstra-virodhaś ca; kumbha-kāro
jāyate, ratha-kāro jāyata ity-ādi-śravaṇāt / api ca sarveṣāṃ kāryāṇāṃ śarīra-ādīnāṃ ca sattva-ādi-guṇa-kārya-rūpa-sukha-ādy-anvaya-darśanena sattva-ādi-mūlatvam avaśya-āśrayaṇīyam / kārya-vaicitrya-hetu-bhūtāḥ kāraṇa-gatā viśeṣās sattva-ādayaḥ; teṣāṃ kāryāṇāṃ tan-mūlatva-āpādanaṃ tad-yukta-puruṣa-antaḥkaraṇa-vikāra-dvāreṇa, puruṣasya ca tad-yogaḥ karma-mūlaḥ --- iti kārya-viśeṣa-ārambhāya eva jñāna-śaktivat kartuḥ karma-saṃbandhaḥ kārya-hetutvena eva avaśya-āśrayanīyaḥ; jñāna-śakti-vaicitryasya ca karma-mūlatvāt / icchāyāḥ kārya-ārambha-hetutve 'pi viṣaya-viśeṣa-viśeṣitāyās tasyās sattva-āi-mūlakatvena karma-saṃbandho 'varjanīyaḥ / ataḥ kṣetra-jñā eva kartāraḥ, na tad-vilakṣaṇaḥ kaścid anumānāt sidhyati / bhavanti ca prayogāḥ --- tanu-bhuvana-ādi kṣetra-jña-kartṛkam, kāryatvāt, ghaṭavat / īśvaraḥ kartā na bhavati, prayojana-śūnyatvāt, mukta-ātmavat / īśvaraḥ kartā na bhavati, a-śarīratvāt, tadvad eva / na ca kṣetra-jñānāṃ sva-śarīra-adhiṣṭhāne vyabhicāraḥ, tatra apy anādes sūkṣma-śarīrasta sad-bhāvāt/ vimati-viṣayaḥ kālo na loka-śūnyaḥ, kālatvāt, vartamāna-kālavad iti /

body.text: api ca, kim īśvaras saśarīro 'śarīro vā kāryaṃ karoti ? na tāvad aśarīraḥ; aśarīrasya kartṛtvānupalabdheḥ / mānasāny api kāryāṇi saśarīrasyaiva bhavanti; manaso nityatve 'pi aśarīreṣu mukteṣu tatkāryādarśanāt / nāpi saśarīraḥ; vikalpāsahatvāt -- taccharīraṃ kiṃ nityam utānityam ? na tāvan nityam; sāvayavasya tasya nityatve jagato 'pi nityatvāvirodhād īśvarāsiddheḥ / nāpy anityam; tadvyatiriktasya taccharīrahetos tadānīm abhāvāt / svayam eva hetur iti cen na; aśarīrasya tadayogāt; anyena śarīreṇa saśarīra iti cen na; anavasthānāt /
body.translated_text: Moreover, does <s>Īśvara</s> (God) act with a body or without a body? Not without a body, since agency is not observed in a bodiless [being]. Even mental activities belong only to an embodied [being]; for even though <s>manas</s> (mind) is eternal, its effects are not seen in liberated souls who are bodiless. Nor is he embodied, because no alternative is tenable—is that body permanent or impermanent? Not permanent, for if that body, which has parts, were permanent, then there would be no contradiction in the permanence of the world also, and [the need for] <s>Īśvara</s> would not be established. Nor is it impermanent, since there would be no cause for that body other than [Īśvara] himself at that time. If it be said that he himself is the cause [of his body]—no, because this is impossible for a bodiless being. If it be said that he is embodied by means of another body—no, because of infinite regress.

children.text: api ca, kim īśvaras sa-śarīro 'śarīro vā kāryaṃ karoti ? na tāvad a-śarīraḥ; a-śarīrasya kartṛtva-anupalabdheḥ / mānasāny api kāryāṇi sa-śarīrasya eva bhavanti; manaso nityatve 'pi a-śarīreṣu mukteṣu tat-kārya-adarśanāt / na api sa-śarīraḥ; vikalpa-asahatvāt --- tac-charīraṃ kiṃ nityam uta anityam ? na tāvan nityam; sa-avayavasya tasya nityatve jagato 'pi nityatva-avirodhād īśvara-asiddheḥ / na apy anityam; tad-vyatiriktasya tac-charīra-hetos tadānīm abhāvāt / svayam eva hetur iti cen na; a-śarīrasya tad-ayogāt; anyena śarīreṇa sa-śarīra iti cen na; anavasthānāt /

body.text: sa kiṃ savyāpāro nirvyāpāro vā ? aśarīratvād eva na savyāpāraḥ / nāpi nirvyāpāraḥ kāryaṃ karoti muktātmavat / kāryaṃ jagad icchāmātravyāpārakartṛkam ity ucyamāne pakṣasyāprasiddhaviśeṣaṇatvam, dṛṣṭāntasya ca sādhyahīnatā /
body.translated_text: Is he active or inactive? Because he is without a body, he is not active. Nor does an inactive [being] produce an effect, like a liberated soul. If it is said that the world-effect is produced by the mere activity of will—then the qualifier of the thesis [i.e., that Īśvara creates] is unestablished, and the example is lacking in what is to be proved.

children.text: sa kiṃ sa-vyāpāro nirvyāpāro vā ? a-śarīratvād eva na sa-vyāpāraḥ / na api nirvyāpāraḥ kāryaṃ karoti mukta-ātmavat / kāryaṃ jagad icchā-mātra-vyāpāra-kartṛkam ity ucyamāne pakṣasya aprasiddha-viśeṣaṇatvam, dṛṣṭāntasya ca sādhya-hīnatā /

body.text: ato darśanānuguṇyeneśvarānumānaṃ darśanānuguṇyaparāhatam iti śāstraikapramāṇakaḥ parabrahmabhūtas sarveśvaraḥ puruṣottamaḥ / śāstraṃ tu sakaletarapramāṇaparidṛṣṭasamastavastuvisajātīyaṃ sārvajñyasatyasaṃkalpatvādimiśrānavadhikātiśayāparimitodāraguṇasāgaraṃ nikhilaheyapratyanīkasvarūpaṃ pratipādayatīti na pramāṇāntarāvasitavastusādharmyaprayuktadoṣagandhaprasaṅgaḥ /
body.translated_text: Therefore, the inference of <s>Īśvara</s>, following the analogy of [ordinary] perception, is overturned by [the limitations of] that same perceptual analogy. Hence, the Supreme Lord, the <s>Puruṣottama</s> (Supreme Person), who is the Supreme <s>Brahman</s>, is known through scripture (<s>śāstra</s>) alone as the sole valid means of knowledge. And scripture declares [him to be] entirely different in kind from all objects ascertained by all other means of knowledge—an ocean of unlimited, unsurpassed, immeasurably generous qualities, blended with omniscience (<s>sārvajñya</s>), infallible will (<s>satyasaṃkalpa</s>), and the like—whose essential nature is opposed to all that is defective. Thus there is not even a trace of the defects that might be imputed through similarity to objects established by other means of knowledge.

children.text: ato darśana-ānuguṇyenā iśvara-anumānaṃ darśana-ānuguṇya-parāhatam iti śāstra eka-pramāṇakaḥ para-brahma-bhūtas sarva-īśvaraḥ puruṣa-uttamaḥ / śāstraṃ tu sakala-itara-pramāṇa-paridṛṣṭa-samasta-vastu-visajātīyaṃ sārvajñya-satya-saṃkalpatva-ādi-miśra-anavadhika-atiśaya-aparimita-udāra-guṇa-sāgaraṃ nikhila-heya-pratyanīka-sva-rūpaṃ pratipādayati iti na pramāṇa-antara-avasita-vastu-sādharmya-prayukta-doṣa-gandha-prasaṅgaḥ /

body.text: yat tu nimittopādānayor aikyam ākāśāder niravayavadravyasya kāryatvaṃ cānupalabdham aśakyapratipādanam ity uktam, tad apy aviruddham iti prakṛtiś ca pratijñādṛṣṭāntānuparodhāt, na viyadaśruter ity atra pratipādayiṣyate / ataḥ pramāṇāntarāgocaratvena śāstraikaviṣayatvād yato vā imāni bhūtānīti vākyam uktalakṣaṇaṃ brahma pratipādayatīti siddham //1,1.3//
body.translated_text: As for what was said—that the identity of the efficient and material causes, and the production of partless substances such as <s>ākāśa</s> (space), is unobserved and impossible to establish—this too is not contradictory, as will be demonstrated in [the sūtras] '<s>prakṛtiś ca pratijñādṛṣṭāntānuparodhāt</s>' (And [Brahman is] the material cause, since there is no contradiction to the thesis and the example) and '<s>na viyadaśruteḥ</s>' (Not space, because of scriptural statement). Therefore, since [Brahman] is beyond the scope of other means of knowledge and is the exclusive subject of scripture alone, it is established that the sentence 'from which indeed these beings [are born]' teaches <s>Brahman</s> of the described characteristics. // 1.1.3 //

children.text: yat tu nimitta-upādānayor aikyam ākāśa-āder niravayava-dravyasya kāryatvaṃ ca anupalabdham aśakya-pratipādanam ity uktam, tad apy aviruddham iti prakṛtiś ca pratijñā-dṛṣṭānta-anuparodhāt, na viyad-aśruter ity atra pratipādayiṣyate / ataḥ pramāṇa-antara-agocaratvena śāstra-eka-viṣayatvād yato vā imāni bhūtāni iti vākyam ukta-lakṣaṇaṃ brahma pratipādayati iti siddham //1,1.3//
